conventions: The parkour moves, written as the athletic vocabulary's units are (units.json beside this file): an entry state, timed phases, an exit state, and the tell, commitment and recovery a contest reads. Two postures join the athletic ones: hang, hanging from a ledge or a bar, and down, low on the floor or squatting behind cover. Expressions are evaluated by parkour.physics(), which adds the surface moves of humanities/sport/surfaces.py to the vocabulary's physics. A move that needs both hands enters with the ball free. Shapes are left to the whole-body round.
evidence: Moves from parkour, freerunning and obstacle courses, timed by the surface moves' screens in surfaces.py: pushes on the jump's force-velocity profile, friction on surfaces, an assumed arm pull, and the vocabulary's physics. No move has been solved on the whole body, measured in low gravity or performed.

families.parkour: Moves that use walls, ledges, boxes and bars to get across an arena

units.name: speed vault
units.source: parkour's speed vault; a hurdler's hand-assisted clearance
units.description: Running at a box, one hand plants on its top and the legs swing over beside it; the body crosses low and keeps its speed.
units.lunar: adapted: over a box 1 m high and 1.5 m long at 3 m/s, the flight takes 1.5 s from a take-off 1.4 m before the box (Earth 0.8 s from 0.4 m), and the run's speed is kept. The hand holds a sixth of the weight, so a lunar runner can also clear a 1.2 m box, where the model's Earth runner cannot.
checks: the centre of mass clears the top with the hand's support
the take-off within the force-velocity profile

units.name: kong vault
units.description: Diving at a box, both hands plant on its top and push, and the body passes over between the arms, feet first to land.
units.lunar: adapted: both hands push forward off the box's top, so the body leaves 1.4 m/s faster than it came (4.4 m/s from a 3 m/s run) and lands 3.5 m beyond the box after 1.7 s (Earth 1.0 s and 1.8 m). It is the vault that adds speed.
checks: the centre of mass clears the top with both hands' support
the hands' forward push inside the top's friction cone

units.name: tic-tac
units.source: parkour's tic-tac; a basketball player's foot off the stanchion
units.description: A foot meets a wall on the run and pushes off it, turning the travel sharply away from the wall.
units.lunar: native: running at 3 m/s and meeting a wall 45 degrees from its normal, a foot's push changes the velocity by 5.3 m/s in 0.38 s and turns the travel 101 degrees, or up to 6.7 m/s and 168 degrees. That is twelve times what one floor stance can change (0.43 m/s), and the floor's cut through the same turn needs a 2.1 m bounce and 6.8 s. On Earth the wall gives twice a stance's change. On the Moon walls make the sharp turns.
checks: the push inside the wall's friction cone, holding the body's height
the yield within the leg's stroke and force

units.name: wall run
units.source: parkour's wall run (run-up); a steeplechaser's step onto the barrier
units.description: A run meets a wall head on and the feet step up it, the wall's grip lifting the body; kicking off the last step throws it up and away.
units.lunar: native: running into a wall at 3 m/s and kicking off it throws the body 7.5 m up, the hands to 9.7 m, after 0.44 s on the wall (Earth 1.2 m and 3.4 m, about what parkour runners reach). Stepping up and staying at the wall lifts it 1.8 m (Earth 0.3 m). Either way the body is then held to its arc for up to 3 s.
checks: each step inside the wall's friction cone
the centre of mass within the wall's reach

units.name: cat leap
units.description: From a jump or a fall the hands catch a ledge or a wall's top and the feet meet the wall below; the body hangs.
units.lunar: adapted: the arms catch a descent of up to 2.8 m/s, a 2.4 m drop above the catch (Earth 1.7 m/s and 0.15 m); a 1 m/s descent asks a third of an Earth body weight of them (Earth 1.2).
checks: the arms' force at the catch within their pull

units.name: climb up
units.source: parkour's climb up (muscle-up onto a wall)
units.description: From a hang the arms pull and press the body up over the edge until it crouches on the top.
units.lunar: adapted: the arms throw the body up over the edge in a fifth of a second, but it then coasts to rest on gravity's clock, 1.5 s in all against Earth's 1.0 s; the stop, not the lift, is slow.
checks: the rise stopping no faster than g
the arms within their pull

units.name: precision jump
units.description: A jump across a gap lands both feet on a narrow edge and stops there, without stepping on.
units.lunar: adapted: a 1 m gap to a 0.2 m edge takes 1.1 s in the air and sticks; the widest gap the body can still stop on is 5.8 m (Earth 1.27 m), the landing's braking limited by the balance over the edge rather than its grip.
checks: the landing's braking within the balance over a narrow edge and its grip

units.name: drop and roll
units.source: parkour's drop and roll; a judoka's forward roll
units.description: Off a level the body drops, lands on the balls of the feet into a deep bend and rolls over a shoulder to run on.
units.lunar: adapted: a 3 m drop lands at 3.1 m/s, like a 0.5 m drop on Earth: 1.4 Earth body weights in the legs, or 0.5 with a roll (Earth 8.5 and 3.1). The fall takes 1.9 s and the roll 0.9 s.
checks: the landing's push spread over the legs' stroke and the roll

units.name: lache
units.source: parkour's lache (bar swing and release); a gymnast's release from the bar
units.description: Caught on the run, a bar swings the body forward and lets it go into a long flight.
units.lunar: native in its hazard: caught at 3 m/s, a bar swings the body out at 2.9 m/s into a 1.9 s flight that lands 5.4 m beyond it (Earth 1.3 m), and the swing's turn spins it 308 degrees on the way unless its shape slows it (Earth 51). The swing's period is 5.4 s (Earth 2.2 s).
checks: energy and angular momentum through the swing
the arms within their pull

units.name: slide into cover
units.source: a baseball slide; paintball's slide into a bunker
units.description: From a run the body drops into a feet-first slide along the floor and comes to rest low.
units.lunar: native: dropping into a slide takes 0.83 s, the sink running on gravity's clock, and from 3 m/s the slide then runs 4.7 m for 3.8 s (Earth 0.36 m in 0.43 s). A lunar slide carries a player 7 m into cover, low the whole way after the sink.
checks: the sink no faster than g
the slide at the clothing's grip

units.name: pull down behind cover
units.source: a lunar move: the hands on cover pull the body down
units.description: With the hands on the top of cover the arms pull the body down behind it, faster than it can sink by its weight.
units.lunar: native: with the hands on cover the arms pull the body down 0.5 m in 0.36 s, where its weight alone would take 0.83 s. On Earth the pull saves 0.08 s; on the Moon it halves the duck.
checks: the arms within their pull
the legs' braking

units.name: rise from low
units.source: getting up from a slide or a squat behind cover
units.description: From low behind cover the legs raise the body into the ready crouch and stop it there.
units.lunar: adapted: rising from low behind cover into the ready crouch takes 0.75 s, the stop on gravity's clock (Earth 0.43 s).
checks: the rise stopping no faster than g
